title: Ledger and Typewriter
premise: In 1938, Ada Yarrow carried coded ledgers out of a collapsing republic, and the silence she kept about what those codes cost her family has defined twenty years of exile. When a stranger named Elias Vann arrives with letters in the handwriting of her brother Tomas—officially dead since the evacuation—Ada must decide whether to trust him with the truth of who betrayed their escape route. As Vann is drawn into Ada's fractured household and hunted by the man who sold them out, he discovers the last berth on a repatriation ship can save only one of three people who each hold a piece of the ledger's secret. In the end, Ada chooses truth over loyalty, exposing the betrayer at the cost of her own safe passage, while Vann sails with the ledger—and Tomas, alive after all—toward a home none of them expected.
about_author: Xanthe Whitlock is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from interwar Europe before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule, much like history repeating itself.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Ada Yarrow, now a bookkeeper in a port city, catalogs her late mother's effects and finds a burned corner of an old ledger she thought destroyed. Her POV establishes the discipline of her silences. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Elias Vann, a translator with no country left, arrives claiming to carry letters written by Ada's brother Tomas—dead for twenty years. Told from Vann's POV; his charm barely covers his desperation. Beat: the past knocks loudly.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Dead
chapters.summary: Ada examines the letters and recognizes Tomas's hand unmistakably, including a childhood code only siblings would know. Her POV. Beat: grief reopened like a wound that never closed.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Carried
chapters.summary: Vann recounts how he found the letters among a dead courier's effects, omitting that he was paid to deliver them. His POV, guilt simmering. Beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: The Household of Silences
chapters.summary: Ada introduces Vann to her household: her sharp-tongued aunt Marta and her ward Nell, who suspects everything. Ada's POV. Beat: belonging offered cautiously.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback through Ada's memory: the night of the evacuation, the berth she gave up, the code she memorized and burned. Ada's POV. Beat: the origin of her loyalty to silence.

chapters.title: The Man Who Sold the Route
chapters.summary: Vann identifies the letters' second recipient: Colonel Brecht, the officer who betrayed the escape network and now trades in secrets. Vann's POV. Beat: the hunt has two directions.

chapters.title: Nell Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Nell, too perceptive for her own safety, confronts Vann about why he really came. Vann's POV, disarmed by her directness. Beat: truth leaks through the youngest eyes.

chapters.title: Marta's Warning
chapters.summary: Marta privately tells Ada that men like Vann arrive with debts attached, and that she recognized Brecht's name from the old days. Marta's POV. Beat: loyalty tested by fear.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: A second letter arrives, this one addressed to Ada directly, asking her to bring 'the remainder' to the harbor office. Ada's POV. Beat: hope curdling into trap-sense.

chapters.title: Brecht at the Consulate
chapters.summary: Vann attends a consular reception and sees Brecht alive, powerful, and watching him back. Vann's POV. Beat: the predator knows the prey's face.

chapters.title: What Remainder Means
chapters.summary: Ada decodes the letter using Tomas's childhood cipher and realizes 'the remainder' is the missing half of the ledger—the half naming every traitor. Ada's POV. Beat: she has been carrying it all along.

chapters.title: The Berth Announcement
chapters.summary: News breaks: a repatriation ship will sail in ten days with limited berths for verified former citizens. The household calculates who qualifies. Nell's POV. Beat: hope as arithmetic.

chapters.title: Vann's Debt Comes Due
chapters.summary: Brecht's men find Vann and remind him of his payment: deliver Ada and the ledger, or answer for forged papers. Vann's POV. Beat: the noose he tied himself.

chapters.title: Ada Confronts Vann
chapters.summary: Ada, having noticed his forged travel documents, demands the whole truth. He confesses partially—hired courier, not hired hunter. Ada's POV. Beat: betrayal and tenderness in the same breath.

chapters.title: Tomas's Last Night, Retold
chapters.summary: Vann shares what the letters reveal: Tomas survived the betrayal, was imprisoned, and wrote these letters believing Ada could still be reached. Vann's POV. Beat: the dead brother breathes.

chapters.title: Marta Makes a Call
chapters.summary: Marta secretly contacts an old resistance contact to verify Brecht's movements, risking exposure. Marta's POV. Beat: loyalty choosing its side at last.

chapters.title: The Harbor Office Trap
chapters.summary: Against her judgment, Ada scouts the harbor office and confirms Brecht expects her there—with soldiers. Ada's POV. Beat: fear sharpened into strategy.

chapters.title: Nell Follows
chapters.summary: Nell tails Ada and is nearly caught by Brecht's clerk, forcing Vann to intervene and burn his cover. Nell's POV. Beat: innocence costs cover stories.

chapters.title: Divided House
chapters.summary: The household argues over whether to run, hide, or meet Brecht. Each wants the berth for someone else. Rotating close third on all four. Beat: love as competing claims.

chapters.title: The Cipher's Third Layer
chapters.summary: Ada discovers the ledger's code contains a third layer—a confession Tomas wrote naming Brecht and, painfully, their father's collaboration. Ada's POV. Beat: inheritance as burden.

chapters.title: Father's Name
chapters.summary: Marta admits she knew about Ada's father's collaboration and stayed silent to protect the children. Marta's POV. Beat: the oldest silence cracks.

chapters.title: Brecht's Offer
chapters.summary: Brecht summons Ada openly: the ledger for three berths on the ship, no questions. Ada's POV. Beat: temptation priced exactly right.

chapters.title: Vann Refuses His Paymaster
chapters.summary: Vann tells Brecht the deal is off, knowing it signs his own warrant. Vann's POV. Beat: redemption as self-destruction.

chapters.title: Nell's Discovery
chapters.summary: Nell finds the hidden ledger half and reads enough to understand her guardians' whole history. Nell's POV. Beat: childhood ends quietly.

chapters.title: The Choice Framed
chapters.summary: Three berths, four people: Ada, Vann, Nell, and possibly Tomas if he lives. Ada drafts and burns three different plans overnight. Ada's POV. Beat: arithmetic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Marta Stays Behind
chapters.summary: Marta reveals she cannot sail—her papers name her as a collaborator's widow—and asks only to be remembered honestly. Marta's POV. Beat: dignity without rescue.

chapters.title: Tomas Is Alive
chapters.summary: A telegram confirms Tomas survived and is being held near the harbor as leverage against the ledger. Vann's POV. Beat: joy weaponized.

chapters.title: The Exchange Planned
chapters.summary: Ada plans to trade herself and the ledger for Tomas, secretly arranging for Vann and Nell to take the other berths. Ada's POV. Beat: love as logistics.

chapters.title: Nell Refuses the Berth
chapters.summary: Nell discovers the plan and refuses to leave, forcing the first honest family argument in twenty years. Nell's POV. Beat: belonging means staying.

chapters.title: Brecht Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Brecht, tipped by a clerk, moves up the exchange and seals the harbor district. Vann's POV. Beat: time runs out audibly.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Ship
chapters.summary: The household spends its last quiet night sharing truths—the evacuation, the father, the silences kept 'to keep people safe.' Rotating POVs. Beat: grace before the fall.

chapters.title: Ledger and Typewriter
chapters.summary: Ada retypes the ledger's contents into duplicate pages, keeping the original to surrender and the copy to smuggle. Title chapter; Ada's POV. Beat: truth made portable.

chapters.title: The Exchange at Pier Nine
chapters.summary: At the pier, Ada surrenders the original ledger; soldiers produce Tomas—but Brecht reneges on the berths. Ada's POV. Beat: the trap springs.

chapters.title: Marta's Gambit
chapters.summary: Marta arrives with her resistance contact and evidence of Brecht's wartime dealings, trading her own freedom to force the berths open. Marta's POV. Beat: the last silence spent.

chapters.title: Which Family Member Sails
chapters.summary: Climax: with one berth left and soldiers closing in, Ada puts Tomas aboard, gives Vann her own papers, and stays behind with Nell hidden in the crowd. Ada's POV. Beat: choice as identity.

chapters.title: What Brecht Reads
chapters.summary: Brecht opens the surrendered ledger and finds Ada's retyped pages naming him—she gave him a forgery and mailed the true copy to three newspapers. Vann's POV from the departing ship. Beat: truth outruns loyalty.

chapters.title: The Ship Departs
chapters.summary: From the rail, Vann watches Ada vanish into the crowd as Brecht's world begins collapsing around him ashore. Vann's POV. Beat: salvation with salt in it.

chapters.title: Two Years Later
chapters.summary: Postwar: Vann and Tomas find Ada and Nell living under new names; the published ledger has cleared the family's name and condemned Brecht. Vann's POV. Beat: reunion earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Silence Ends
chapters.summary: Ada finally tells the whole story aloud, unburned and unedited, and begins writing it down beside the old typewriter. Ada's POV closes the book. Beat: belonging found in telling the truth.
